In this role, you will work closely with TERC scientists to develop and apply tools and studies that help us understand chemical Adsorption, Distribution, Metabolism and Excretion (ADME) and other toxicological endpoints. This is a laboratory-based position, and the successful candidate is expected to be actively involved in studies and research projects, including in vivo mammalian (e.g., rat) studies and in vitro systems (e.g., metabolism, plasma protein binding). Work includes experimental design, study conduct, interpretation of results, and evaluation of assay performance including the identification of biomarkers for toxicological assessments.
cond_0018.responsibilities:
Provide science leadership and hands-on support in conducting laboratory research studies to coordinate the design, conduct, and reporting of assigned studies
Work with the team to design and conduct studies examining toxicokinetic parameters of interest (e.g., intrinsic clearance, species comparative metabolism, plasma protein binding)
Support instrument set up, maintenance, and troubleshooting, including coordinating with vendors
Contribute to and help oversee in vivo study operations including dosing, sample collection, necropsy, and animal husbandry activities
Work alongside the study team and draw on broader expertise to deliver high quality scientific results aligned with business and regulatory needs
Collaborate on technical solutions through hands-on experimentation and problem solving for investigative research
Share findings clearly and concisely both internally and externally, including through publications and presentations
Conduct studies using Good Laboratory Practices (GLP)
Understand and follow applicable EH&S standards, policies, and procedures. Support a culture of safety by modeling safe behaviors and helping promote safe work habits across the team
cond_0018.requirements:
A minimum of a bachelor's degree in toxicology, pharmacology, biology, or a related field
A minimum of 2 years of experience conducting ADME/toxicokinetic studies or related experience
A minimum requirement for this [Location masked] based position is the ability to work legally in [Location masked]. No visa sponsorship/support is available for this position, including for any type of permanent residency (green card) process
Masters and/or Ph.D. In toxicology, pharmacology, biology, or a related field
Experience conducting in vivo and in vitro ADME/toxicokinetic studies
Knowledge of organosilicon chemistry is beneficial
Knowledge of common metabolic mechanisms and processes
Knowledge of organic chemistry, polymer chemistry, and/or analytical chemistry
Capable of lifting 50 pounds unassisted and should not have any known animal allergies
Able to wear all required personal protective equipment
Proven project management skills. Ability to define scope and deliverables and successfully lead a small to medium project to completion
Strong safety mindset
Strong inclusion, diversity, and equity mindset
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Strong ability to analyze and interpret study results
Strong interpersonal skills. Proactively seeks to understand differences of opinions to resolve
Able to work independently and within a multidisciplinary team setting
Strong work ethic and attention to detail
Interest in solving complex research problems and exploring the unknown
Must be able to work flexible schedules that include occasional weekends, evenings, and holidays during study in-life
Knowledge of or willingness to learn regulatory guideline testing requirements, Good Laboratory Practice (GLP), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and animal welfare standards

cond_0098.intro: We are looking for a Laboratory Study Director to join our Product Safety Research group, part of our Toxicology and Environment Research & Consulting (TERC) Team. In this role, you will own investigative research conducted to ensure the sustainability of our chemistries. You will bring experience and training in toxicology, pharmacology, biology, or a related field, and will take the lead in developing and applying state-of-the-art tools and studies to understand chemical Adsorption, Distribution, Metabolism and Excretion (ADME) and other toxicological endpoints. This is a laboratory-based position where you are expected to drive active involvement in studies and research projects, including in vivo mammalian (e.g., rat) studies and in vitro systems (e.g., metabolism, plasma protein binding). You will own experimental design, study conduct, interpretation of results, and evaluation of assay performance including the identification of biomarkers for toxicological assessments.
cond_0098.responsibilities:
Lead and execute laboratory research studies, taking full ownership of design, conduct, and reporting on assigned studies
Direct studies to examine toxicokinetic parameters of interest (e.g., intrinsic clearance, species comparative metabolism, plasma protein binding)
Take charge of instrument set up, maintenance, and troubleshooting, including managing coordination with vendors
Oversee and execute in vivo study operations including dosing, sample collection, necropsy, and animal husbandry activities
Lead the study team and draw on broader expertise to deliver high quality scientific results aligned with business and regulatory needs
Develop and implement technical solutions through hands-on experimentation and problem solving for investigative research
Deliver clear, concise communications both internally and externally, including publications and presentations
Execute studies under Good Laboratory Practices (GLP)
Understand and follow applicable EH&S standards, policies, and procedures. Set the example in safety behaviors and champion safe work habits

cond_0262.intro: We are looking for a Laboratory Study Director to join our team. Specifically, we are looking for someone with experience and training in toxicology, pharmacology, biology, or a related field. The candidate will work closely with TERC scientists in developing and applying state-of-the-art tools and studies to understand chemical Adsorption, Distribution, Metabolism and Excretion (ADME) and other toxicological end points. This is a laboratory-based position, and the successful candidate is expected to be actively involved in studies and research projects, including in vivo mammalian (e.g., rat) studies and in vitro systems (e.g., metabolism, plasma protein binding). Activities include experimental design, study conduct, interpretation of results, and evaluation of assay performance including the identity of biomarkers for toxicological assessments.
cond_0262.responsibilities:
Provides science leadership and hands-on experience in conducting laboratory research studies to design, conduct and report on assigned studies
Designs and conducts studies to examine toxicokinetic parameters of interest (e.g., intrinsic clearance, species comparative metabolism, plasma protein binding)
Provides support for instrument set up, maintenance, and troubleshooting, including working with vendors
Oversees and demonstrates experience in in-vivo study operations including dosing, sample collection, necropsy and animal husbandry activities
Leads study team and leverages broader expertise to deliver high quality scientific results that are aligned with business and regulatory needs
Develops and implements technical solutions through hands-on experimentation/problem solving for the investigative research
Provides clear, concise communications both internally and externally including publications and presentations
Performs studies using Good Laboratory Practices (GLP)
Understands and follows appropriate EH&S standards, policies, and procedures applicable to their job. Leads by example in the area of safety behaviors and promotes safe work habits
cond_0262.requirements:
A minimum of a bachelor's degree in toxicology, pharmacology, biology or a related field
A minimum of 2 years experience conducting ADME/toxicokinetic studies or related experience
Masters and/or Ph.D. In toxicology, pharmacology, biology or a related field
Experience conducting in vivo and in vitro ADME/toxicokinetic studies
Knowledge of organosilicon chemistry is beneficial
Knowledge of common metabolic mechanisms and processes
Knowledge of organic chemistry, polymer chemistry and/or analytical chemistry
Capable of lifting 50 pounds unassisted and should not have any known animal allergies
Wear all required personal protective equipment
Proven project management skills. Ability to define scope and deliverables, successfully lead a small to medium project to completion
Strong safety mindset
Strong inclusion, diversity and equity mindset
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Strong ability to analyze and interpret study results
Strong interpersonal skills. Proactively seeks to understand differences of opinions to resolve
Work independently and within a multidisciplinary team setting
Strong work ethic and attention to detail
A passion for solving complex research problems and exploring the unknown
Must be able to work flexible schedules that include occasional weekends, evenings and holidays during study in-life.
Knowledge or willingness to learn regulatory guideline testing requirements, Good Laboratory Practice (GLP), standard operating procedures (SOPs) and animal welfare standards

In this role, you will work closely with TERC scientists to develop and apply tools and studies that help us understand chemical Adsorption, Distribution, Metabolism and Excretion (ADME) and other toxicological endpoints. This is a laboratory-based position, and the successful candidate is expected to be actively involved in studies and research projects, including in vivo mammalian (e.g., rat) studies and in vitro systems (e.g., metabolism, plasma protein binding). Work includes experimental design, study conduct, interpretation of results, and evaluation of assay performance including the identification of biomarkers for toxicological assessments.
cond_0270.responsibilities:
Provide science leadership and hands-on support in conducting laboratory research studies to coordinate the design, conduct, and reporting of assigned studies
Work with the team to design and conduct studies examining toxicokinetic parameters of interest (e.g., intrinsic clearance, species comparative metabolism, plasma protein binding)
Support instrument set up, maintenance, and troubleshooting, including coordinating with vendors
Contribute to and help oversee in vivo study operations including dosing, sample collection, necropsy, and animal husbandry activities
Work alongside the study team and draw on broader expertise to deliver high quality scientific results aligned with business and regulatory needs
Collaborate on technical solutions through hands-on experimentation and problem solving for investigative research
Share findings clearly and concisely both internally and externally, including through publications and presentations
Conduct studies using Good Laboratory Practices (GLP)
Understand and follow applicable EH&S standards, policies, and procedures. Support a culture of safety by modeling safe behaviors and helping promote safe work habits across the team
cond_0270.requirements:
A minimum of a bachelor's degree in toxicology, pharmacology, biology, or a related field
A minimum of 2 years of experience conducting ADME/toxicokinetic studies or related experience
A minimum requirement for this [Location masked] based position is the ability to work legally in [Location masked]. No visa sponsorship/support is available for this position, including for any type of permanent residency (green card) process
Masters and/or Ph.D. In toxicology, pharmacology, biology, or a related field
Experience conducting in vivo and in vitro ADME/toxicokinetic studies
Knowledge of organosilicon chemistry is beneficial
Knowledge of common metabolic mechanisms and processes
Knowledge of organic chemistry, polymer chemistry, and/or analytical chemistry
Capable of lifting 50 pounds unassisted and should not have any known animal allergies
Able to wear all required personal protective equipment
Proven project management skills. Ability to define scope and deliverables and successfully lead a small to medium project to completion
Strong safety mindset
Strong inclusion, diversity, and equity mindset
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Strong ability to analyze and interpret study results
Strong interpersonal skills. Proactively seeks to understand differences of opinions to resolve
Able to work independently and within a multidisciplinary team setting
Strong work ethic and attention to detail
Interest in solving complex research problems and exploring the unknown
Must be able to work flexible schedules that include occasional weekends, evenings, and holidays during study in-life

You will work closely with scientists to develop and apply tools and studies to understand chemical Adsorption, Distribution, Metabolism and Excretion (ADME) and other toxicological endpoints. This is a hands-on, laboratory-based position with active involvement in in vivo mammalian (e.g., rat) studies and in vitro systems (e.g., metabolism, plasma protein binding). Work includes experimental design, study conduct, interpretation of results, and evaluation of assay performance including identification of biomarkers for toxicological assessments.
cond_0510.responsibilities:
Provide science leadership and hands-on experience conducting laboratory research studies — designing, running, and reporting on assigned studies
Design and conduct studies to examine toxicokinetic parameters of interest (e.g., intrinsic clearance, species comparative metabolism, plasma protein binding)
Support instrument set up, maintenance, and troubleshooting, including staying in regular contact with vendors to resolve issues
Oversee in vivo study operations including dosing, sample collection, necropsy, and animal husbandry activities
Lead the study team and connect regularly with broader scientific expertise to deliver high-quality results aligned with business and regulatory needs
Develop and implement technical solutions through hands-on experimentation and problem solving
Communicate clearly and directly, both internally and externally, including through publications and presentations
Conduct studies under Good Laboratory Practices (GLP)
Understand and follow applicable EH&S standards, policies, and procedures; lead by example on safety behaviors and actively promote safe work habits within the team
cond_0510.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in toxicology, pharmacology, biology, or a related field
At least 2 years of experience conducting ADME/toxicokinetic studies or related work
Ability to work legally in [Location masked]; no visa sponsorship or support is available, including for permanent residency (green card) processes
Knowledge of common metabolic mechanisms and processes
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Strong ability to analyze and interpret study results
Strong interpersonal skills; proactively seeks to understand differences of opinion to resolve them
Ability to work independently and within a multidisciplinary team
Strong work ethic and attention to detail
Ability to work flexible schedules that include occasional weekends, evenings, and holidays during study in-life
Capable of lifting 50 pounds unassisted, no known animal allergies, and able to wear all required personal protective equipment
Preferred Requirements
Master's and/or Ph.D. In toxicology, pharmacology, biology, or a related field
Experience conducting both in vivo and in vitro ADME/toxicokinetic studies
Knowledge of organic chemistry, polymer chemistry, and/or analytical chemistry
Knowledge of organosilicon chemistry
Proven project management skills; ability to define scope and deliverables and lead a small to medium project to completion
Strong safety mindset
Strong inclusion, diversity, and equity mindset
Interest in solving complex research problems
Knowledge of, or willingness to learn, regulatory guideline testing requirements, GLP, SOPs, and animal welfare standards
